title: R3-W2 carry-forward, now mechanically proven: the pullback_yields app7 leg still writes the dev's real ~/.pp-settings.bin on every odin test run
evidence: pullback_test.odin:286: "effect_settings_adjust(&app7, &app7.input, rnd.SETTINGS_ROW_PULLBACK, 0)" with no settings_path_override set. settings.odin:242-245: "p := app.settings_path_override / if p == "" { / p = settings_path() / }" — effect_settings_adjust ends "settings_save_app(app)" unconditionally. Proof: before/after `odin test app`, ~/.pp-settings.bin mtime moved to the run minute; xxd: "00000000: 5002 0000 0000 00" (v2, palette 0, motion 0, scale 0, pullback OFF).
detail: settings_save_app's own comment says "a test must never touch it" — every native test run (both release and PP_DEBUG legs) resets the dev's real settings to defaults-plus-pullback-OFF.
recommended_fix: Set app7.settings_path_override to a tmp_settings_path()-style temp file before effect_settings_adjust (the exec-level adjust-test pattern already in this repo).

title: R3-W3 carry-forward: pullback_feed still caps spawn-event mapping at 8 ids — a 9+ spawn frame silently returns and skips the pullback
evidence: "ids: [8]u32 / found := rnd.camera_newest_terminals(&app.state.topology, n_spawns, ids[:]) / if found != n_spawns { / return // defensive — every spawn event has a live terminal by construction / }"
detail: camera_newest_terminals stops at len(ids)=8; a genuine seed inside a 9+ catch-up burst is silently dropped. Unreachable via current data (interval 80 vs 5-tick frame cap) but interval is balance.json data.
recommended_fix: Clamp n_spawns to the buffer size and map the newest 8 (newest-first walk keeps a truncated mapping correct for the newest seed), or size the buffer to the max same-frame spawn count.

title: R3-W4 carry-forward: the W7 same-window exclusion still depends unstated on terminal_spawn_interval_ticks exceeding the frame tick cap — nothing asserts it
evidence: main.odin: "window_lo := ids[n_spawns - 1] / window_hi := ids[0] + 1" (derived from the frame slice). core/growth.odin:523: "if tick % cat.balance.terminal_spawn_interval_ticks != 0 {" — no assert anywhere ties the interval to the per-frame tick cap.
detail: If balance.json ever sets interval <= 5, two spawns share a frame and the frame-level exclusion hides the first from the second's plan-time view — view classification diverges (false SEEDs). Inert today, wrong when data moves.
recommended_fix: Assert interval > max ticks-per-frame where balance loads, or derive the exclusion window from terminal_spawn_interval_ticks instead of the frame's spawn-id span.

title: R3-N1 carry-forward: the stale-latch guard still appends a synthetic Mouse_Release without clearing inp.panning — with placement armed it re-fires every frame and can commit a placement
evidence: "} else if pan_latch_stale(inp.panning, rl.IsMouseButtonDown(.LEFT)) { ... append(&inp.events, Device_Event(Mouse_Release{pos = pos, button = .Left}))" — no inp.panning write in the branch. mouse.odin:373 pan branch requires "placing_eff < 0"; mouse.odin:405-415 placement branch emits "Place_Release{pos = release_pos}" on any has_release.
detail: While the latch is stranded and placement is armed, the pan branch never runs so nothing clears panning: a synthetic release is appended every frame, and it reaches the placement branch as Place_Release.
recommended_fix: Clear inp.panning inside the stale-guard branch itself (the synthesized release's purpose is closing the latch) before appending the event.

title: R3-N2 carry-forward: camera_pullback_target comment still claims the clamp is 'a no-op for a zoom-out' — contradicted by its own B1 pin and false in general
evidence: "At z_to=1.0 / the clamp pins both axes to the world center; at any z_to the clamp is / a no-op for a zoom-out (the target half-extents are wider), so the" — the file's own pin moves cy 585→390 on a zoom-out to z_to=1.0, and a center valid at a higher zoom can sit outside the narrower target-zoom band for any z_to.
detail: The sentence directly contradicts the preceding floor sentence and the general edge-pan case; the code is right, the comment's mechanism is wrong. Unchanged from r3.
recommended_fix: Reword: the clamp is a no-op for a zoom-out EXCEPT when the current center falls outside the target-zoom band (always at the 1.0 floor) — the B1 contract.

title: R3-N9 carry-forward: the Pan executor case still has no draw guard — a second finger mid-touch-draw pans the camera, unlike the mouse path
evidence: "case Pan: ... if inp.on_pan != nil { / inp.on_pan(inp.user, inp, v.dx, v.dy) / }" — no inp.drag.active check and no comment declaring the co-fire intentional; mouse_map's pan branch gates on "!drag_eff" (mouse.odin:373).
detail: A two-finger pan during an in-progress touch draw pans mid-gesture (preview re-snaps; worst case jitter). The mouse path never co-fires; the asymmetry is undocumented.
recommended_fix: Either suppress Pan while inp.drag.active in the executor, or add a comment declaring the co-fire intentional with the rationale.

title: R3-N10 carry-forward: wheel residue still advances before the ownership decision — NOC-scrolled/blocked wheels pre-charge the accumulator
